Subject: SIG: Fintegrity Capital - questionnaire and evidence request

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our vendor intake we'd like to collect a completed SIG questionnaire and supporting evidence. Attached is our Fintegrity SIG template (v3). Our audit team would like to receive the completed questionnaire and any evidence by EOD May 20 to meet an internal review window.

High level asks:
- Completed SIG (all sections).
- Evidence for network architecture, access control, and data retention policies (PDFs/screenshots fine).
- If any question cannot be answered with standard controls, please mark as an exception and provide compensating controls + timeline for remediation (if applicable).

Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Alan

Senior Security Analyst
Fintegrity Capital

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Wu <alan.wu@fintegrity.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Fintegrity Capital - questionnaire and evidence request

Alan —

Thanks for sending — we can meet the May 20 window. Team is preparing the responses and collecting evidence. A couple quick notes up front so you have context:

1) Non-standard answers: there are 3 items we cannot give a straight "Yes" to with current product behavior:
   - Network segmentation for shared clusters (multi-tenant control planes): we rely on tenant isolation at the application layer today; dedicated segmentation for control plane-level L2/L3 separation is on our roadmap.
   - In-place encryption key rotation logs: rotation exists but automated rotation audit artifacts are limited for older key versions.
   - Data retention export on demand for sub-account slices: we can provide exports but not yet via self-serve for some aggregated storage backends.

For each of those we will flag an exception in the SIG worksheet and include compensating controls + proposed remediation milestones. Because two of the three are material to network/security posture, I want to surface them to you early.

I will send a draft of our completed SIG and evidence by May 18 for your review. If you'd like a short call to walk the exceptions, I'm happy to schedule one next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SIG-responses-draft.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SIG: Fintegrity Capital - internal: proposed exception language and controls

Team — forwarding Alan's request plus our draft responses. See the proposed exception wording below (I created a short summary to take to security/exec for sign-off). Please review and flag anything you think will block approval.

--- Proposed non-standard answer package (summary) ---
1) Network segmentation (SIG control: segmentation of shared control plane)
   Proposed SIG answer: "No (see compensating controls and roadmap commitment)."
   Compensating controls: tenant-level encryption, strict RBAC, per-tenant runtime limits, continuous workload scanning (CSPM), and mandatory VPC peering for customers with elevated isolation needs.
   Roadmap: committed delivery of dedicated control-plane segmentation option by 2026-12-15.

2) Key rotation audit artifacts
   Proposed SIG answer: "Partial — rotation supported, full automated rotation logs for legacy keys available as a managed request."
   Compensating controls: KMS-backed keys, manual rotation runbook, short key lifetimes, and weekly key integrity checks.
   Roadmap: automated rotation logging improvements by 2026-09-30.

3) Retention/export for sub-account slices
   Proposed SIG answer: "Partial — exports available via support process; self-serve export on roadmap."
   Compensating controls: documented support workflow, signed export attestations, and per-request notifications to customers.
   Roadmap: self-serve export capability by 2026-11-30.

Action requested from Security/Leadership:
- Exec sign-off to mark these as exceptions in the SIG with the compensating controls and roadmap commitments above.
- Agreement that a contractual addendum (small security addendum) documenting the commitments is acceptable to customers in lieu of immediate product changes.

Attachments: SIG-responses-draft.xlsx, evidence_vpc_diagram.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG: Fintegrity Capital - internal: proposed exception language and controls

Marissa / Laura —

I've reviewed the proposed wording and compensating controls. From a Security engineering perspective the items are reasonable as exceptions provided we:

- Narrow the customer-facing language to make clear what is and isn't available today.
- Commit to concrete delivery dates (the ones Marissa listed are fine but let's add Jira ticket references).
- Require a signed security addendum or SLA amendment that includes acceptance criteria and rollback clauses.

Evelyn — can you provide exec sign-off on using a security addendum + the roadmap dates below as the remediation plan? If approved, Legal should prepare a short addendum referencing INF-2487 and FIN-2025-172.

Proposed timeline (add Jira refs):
- Control-plane segmentation: 2026-12-15 (INF-3421)
- Rotation logging improvements: 2026-09-30 (INF-3310)
- Self-serve export: 2026-11-30 (INF-3388)

If we don't get sign-off I'll recommend we either: (a) delay returning the SIG until we can scope a short-term compensating control implementation, or (b) provide the SIG but mark items as "pending remediation" and expect deeper customer negotiation.

Thanks,
Dev
Security Engineering Manager
